results.correct_value: About 4.1 miles one way to High Camp (3.1 mi to the PCT junction at ~6,100 ft, then ~1 mi)
results.evidence: Killen Creek Trail #113 is 3.1 miles to the PCT (Forest Service) and High Camp is about a mile beyond; NW Hiker and Oregon Hikers give 8.2 miles round trip (4.1 one way) and the onX track is 8 miles round trip. Day 1's 8.6 mi is a round-trip-sized figure. The 'High Camp Trail Junction' pin also stored 6,900 ft / 4.5 mi, but the junction is at ~6,100 ft, 3.1 mi (Forest Service ~6,000 ft; guides 6,100 ft). Day 1 gainFt (2,900 vs the sourced ~2,300) is left unchanged because the itinerary gain total cannot yet be reconciled with gain_ft (see Total gain).

Mountain Project gives the route's own gain as 4,700 ft (camp to summit), and a North Cleaver guide gives 'almost 8,000 ft' for the north-side trip car to car, but no source states a car-to-car gain for the Adams Glacier route itself; gain_ft (5,150) and the itinerary sum (7,680) are left for a sourced figure.

Wikipedia puts the Adams Glacier terminus near 7,000 ft (matching approach/approach_variants), but a detailed trip report says parties reached the glacier and roped up at about 8,000 ft (matching the waypoint). The two describe different points (toe vs rope-up) and no two sources agree on the waypoint's meaning.

results.correct_value: Typically ice steps of about 45-50°; some lines/years reach 55-65°
results.evidence: Northwest Mountain School lists the Adams Glacier as snow/ice to 45°, and an Ice and Trail report notes guidebooks put the maximum angle at 45-50° while their left-hand line hit 55-60° touching 65°; a Santiam Alpine Club report describes 50-55° average with a 65° maximum on one feature. So 45-50° is typical and 65° is a real but line-dependent maximum; gear[0] overstated it as 'sustained'.
